segments.label: Fragment A — Amarna EA 356 (Old Babylonian / Middle Babylonian, found at Tell el-Amarna)

i18n.en: […] he rose [before(?)] Anu.

notes.official: Fragment A's first surviving line is fragmentary; the restored sense places Ea (or possibly Adapa) *before Anu* — the cosmographic opening with the sky-god as audience-frame for the apkallu-introduction that follows. The Knudtzon 1915 reading *ina pān* is restored; per the verification-pending caveat, sign-level reconstruction may yet differ from Izre'el 2001's critical edition. The DINGIR-determinative on *Anu* follows the project-wide prose-drop convention.

i18n.en: […] all of heaven knew (him as) one who feared (the gods).

notes.official: Adapa is introduced as the *paradigm god-fearing one* — known across heaven as the one who *fears* (*palāḫu* — reverences) the gods. The verb *pa-li-ḫi i-de* '(he is) known (as) one who fears' establishes Adapa's character-frame: the *fear-of-the-gods* is the foundational disposition of the sage-paradigm. The line is fragmentary; sense well-attested.

i18n.en: The son of Ea brought up [the speech] of his (bitter) mouth —

notes.official: *ma-ru-uš (d)Ea pi-i mar-tu-šu ub-bi-il-am-ma* — 'the son of Ea brought up (the speech) of his (bitter) mouth.' Multiple scholarly readings: the *mouth* (*pû*) is variously construed as (i) the speech-organ that will later effect the wing-breaking curse at B:10-11 — a foreshadowing of the speech-act-efficacy that the central entry `speech-act-efficacy-language-power-of-life-and-death-cross-corpus` documents; (ii) a *crafted feature* of the apkallu-sage (parallel to the wisdom-grant at A:10); (iii) *bitter-eloquence* as the sage-rhetoric. The Translator defaults to the foreshadow-reading following Foster 2005. Per the verification-pending caveat, the precise reconstruction awaits Izre'el 2001.

i18n.en: … as they … (sense uncertain).

notes.official: Sense uncertain across editions; Izre'el 2001 and Foster 2005 differ. The Translator's default is the conservative-deferral with the 'sense uncertain' marker. The verification-pass against Izre'el 2001 should restore the line's exact reading; the lens-discipline is not affected (no theological or lens-risk material at this line).

i18n.en: He (Ea) appointed him — Adapa — as the god-fearing one.

notes.official: *iš-ku-un-šu (d)Adapa pa-li-ḫi* 'he (Ea) set Adapa as the god-fearing one' — the formal-appointment of Adapa as the paradigm-apkallu (the standing-epithet *pa-li-ḫi* 'god-fearing' is repeated from A:2). The verb *šakānu* 'to place, set down' marks the divine-decision-and-appointment; cf. the same verb at B:21 (*Ea amāta išakkan* — Ea *sets down* words to Adapa). See central entry `adapa-apkallu-first-antediluvian-sage-paradigm-cross-corpus` on Adapa's first-of-the-seven-apkallu status.

i18n.en: To all the lands [his] name (went forth).

notes.official: Adapa's renown extends *ana māt ka-li-ši[na]* 'to all the lands' — the formal-extension of the apkallu's name across the inhabited-cosmos. The standard Mesopotamian *kalāmu* 'all, totality' modifier; the apkallu's-renown formula recurs in royal inscriptions and apkallu-tradition material.

i18n.en: He (Ea) made for him the heart of the diadem of heaven.

notes.official: *lib-ba ki-li-il-šu ša šamê e-pu-uš* — Ea makes for Adapa the 'heart of the diadem of heaven'. The phrase is metaphorical and its precise referent is debated: (a) the *heart of the diadem* as the *sage-essence* — restating A:2 / A:5's god-fearing-wisdom; (b) the *diadem of heaven* as Adapa's cosmic-office investiture; (c) a specific cult-emblem associated with Adapa's office at Eridu. The Translator preserves the metaphor untranslated, following Foster 2005.

i18n.en: He made him great; (the gods) [praised(?)] him in their assembly.

notes.official: Ea makes Adapa great; the assembly of the gods praises him. The line is fragmentary at the second half; the *(ig-ga-ar-...) ta-na-am-ma* sense is the gods' praise-assembly response to Adapa's exaltation. The line confirms Adapa's near-divine standing in the heavenly-court — a human among the divine assembly, but as the line that follows (A:10) makes explicit, *without immortality*.

i18n.en: Among the gods […]

notes.official: 'With the gods …' — broken. Adapa stands *it-ti DINGIR.MEŠ* 'with the gods' (with the DINGIR-plural ideogram) despite being human. The line is the apex of the Adapa-among-the-gods elevation-sequence; the next line (A:10) declares the explicit limit on this elevation: wisdom yes, immortality no.

lines.translit: ne-me-qa id-din-šu napišta dāriti ul id-din-šu

i18n.en: Wisdom he gave him; eternal life he did not give him.

notes.official:
**The foundational line of the Adapa composition and one of the single most-quoted lines of Akkadian wisdom-anthropology.** *nēmequ id-din-šu napišta dāriti ul id-din-šu* — 'wisdom he gave him; eternal life he did not give him.' The decoupling of *wisdom* (*nēmequ*) and *eternal life* (*napištu dārītu*) is the structural-pivot of the entire narrative; the food-of-life refusal at B:55-56 enacts cosmically what is theologically announced here. See central entry `nemequ-napishtu-dariti-wisdom-but-not-immortality-paradigm-sage-cross-corpus`.

Cross-corpus, the line parallels Hebrew Gen 3:22 (*hen ha-adam hayah k-achad mimennu la-da'at tov va-ra* 'behold, the human has become like one of us, knowing good and bad' — see existing entry `ke-achad-mimmennu`) in **inverse-pattern**: in Adapa, wisdom is granted-and-immortality-withheld at creation (A:10); in Genesis, wisdom is acquired-by-transgression (Gen 3:7) and immortality is then-barred-by-divine-action (Gen 3:22-24). Both narratives reach the same theological end-state (humans wisdom-bearing-but-mortal) by opposite-direction arcs — the Heidel-Buccellati-Hallo-Kvanvig comparative-mythology framing. **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Christian-Adamic-Fall pre-resolution; the Mesopotamian premise is humans-designed-mortal, not humans-originally-immortal-and-fallen-into-mortality; (ii) no WoH-spin on engineered-mortality-by-design; the *id-din-šu / ul id-din-šu* parataxis is theological-aetiological vocabulary, not engineering-protocol vocabulary; (iii) no Adapa-as-Adam identity claim; the cross-corpus parallel is structural-thematic-comparative-mythology, not etymological-identity.

i18n.en: In those days […] the son of Ea, day by day(?),

notes.official: Narrative-temporal transition: *ina ūmīšu-ma* 'in those days' opens the descriptive-frame for Adapa's daily cult-service at Eridu. The line is fragmentary; the *ūmišammi* 'day by day' adverb sets up the routine that will become the boat-trip-and-South-Wind episode in Fragment B.

lines.translit: ašar (d)Ea ina qereb Eridu(KI) ina ramāni-šu(?) ibšû

i18n.en: (In the place) where Ea dwelt in the midst of Eridu, by his own (creative power).

notes.official: Eridu — Ea's cosmographic-seat — is the *abzu/Apsû*-anchor (the subterranean fresh-water cosmographic-zone of Mesopotamian cosmology; see central entry `abzu-engur-sumerian-subterranean-deep-cross-corpus`). The phrase *ina ramāni-šu(?) ibšû* 'by his own (creative power) he was' marks Ea as cosmically-autonomous in his domain. The cosmographic-frame is the Akkadian-text deployment of the abzu/Apsû tradition. Adapa's standing-epithet *māru ša Eridu* 'son of Eridu' (B:1) and the daily *mê qadišūti* 'pure waters' service (B:3) are anchored here.

i18n.en: […] Adapa, [king(?) of the black-headed people].

notes.official: The closing line of Fragment A, restored: *(d)Adapa [šarru(?) ša ṣalmāt qaqqadi]* '[Adapa, king(?) of] the black-headed people.' The *ṣalmāt qaqqadi* (literally 'black ones of the head': *ṣalmāt* fem. pl. adj. 'black' + *qaqqadi* gen. of *qaqqadu* 'head') is the Akkadian word-by-word semantic-calque of Sumerian *saĝ gig-ga* — the standard Sumerian-Akkadian self-designation for the human population (see existing central entry `sag-gig-ga-black-headed-people-sumerian-self-designation-cross-corpus`, here extended to Akkadian-side activation at this Adapa attestation). The restoration *šarru* 'king' follows Foster 2005 and Izre'el 2001's tentative reading; verification pending.

segments.label: Fragment B — K.8214+ Neo-Assyrian Nineveh (the main narrative)

preceding_lacuna.text: Lacuna of unknown size between Fragments A and B; Fragment B is a Neo-Assyrian Nineveh tablet preserving the main narrative.

i18n.en: [Lacuna of unknown size between Fragments A and B. Fragment B preserves the main Neo-Assyrian narrative as recovered from the Kuyunjik library at Nineveh.]
[…] Adapa, son of Eridu,

notes.official: Fragment B opens with Adapa's standing-epithet *māru ša Eridu* 'son of Eridu' — the apkallu-paradigm's-eponym-link to Ea's cult-city. See central entry `adapa-apkallu-first-antediluvian-sage-paradigm-cross-corpus` on Adapa's first-of-the-seven-apkallu status and Eridu's cosmographic-anchor role.

lines.translit: ina qereb Eridu(KI) (d)Ea ina mayyāli-šu i-nu-uš-šu
lines.cuneiform: 𒀸  𒉣𒆠 𒀭𒀀 𒀸 𒋗 𒄿𒉡𒍑𒋗

i18n.en: In the midst of Eridu, Ea roused him from his couch.

notes.official: *ina qereb Eridu(KI) (d)Ea ina mayyāli-šu i-nu-uš-šu* 'in the midst of Eridu, Ea roused him from his couch'. The master-disciple relationship between Ea and Adapa is foregrounded: Ea wakes Adapa for the day's cult-tasks. The verb *nâšu* 'to rouse, shake' has the technical-cult-service sense of *summon-to-duty*.

i18n.en: [Day by day(?)] in Eridu he [drew(?)] the pure waters.

notes.official: Adapa's daily cult-task: drawing *mê qadišūti* 'the pure waters' for Ea's temple-service at Eridu. The Akkadian *qadišu* is the cognate of Hebrew *qadosh* 'holy'; *mê qadišūti* are the temple-cult fresh-waters from the abzu/Apsû source-zone. See overlay entry `me-qadishuti-pure-cult-waters-akkadian-eridu-temple-service` for the lexical detail. Functional cross-corpus to Hebrew *mayim qedoshim* (Num 5:17 the sotah ordeal-water).

i18n.en: He went up; he embarked upon his boat.

notes.official: Adapa goes up; embarks on his boat. The daily routine of the fishing-trip for Ea's temple-table; the structural-prelude to the South Wind incident.

lines.translit: ina ūmi šuāti ana tâmti dalti(?) ša bāb Eridu(KI) išteni

i18n.en: On that day he set out alone toward the sea-gate of Eridu.

notes.official: *ina ūmi šuāti ana tâmti dalti(?) ša bāb Eridu(KI) išteni* 'on that day he set out alone toward the sea-gate of Eridu'. The *bāb Eridu* sea-gate is Eridu's cosmographic-and-civic-aperture to the Persian Gulf (or, in mythological-cosmography, to the cosmic-deep). The *išteni* 'he set out alone' is the formal-departure-marker.

lines.translit: [X X] elippa-šu nāru ina(?) mê i-šat-tu

i18n.en: […] the current bore his boat upon the waters.

notes.official: The current bears Adapa's boat upon the waters. The line is fragmentary; sense well-attested.

lines.translit: ina libbi tâmti ša rapaš-tum (d)Šūtu(IM.U18.LU) ina pâ-ni-šu it-bi
lines.cuneiform: 𒀸   𒊭 𒌈 𒀭𒅎𒍇𒇻 𒀸 𒉌𒋗 𒀉𒁉

i18n.en: In the midst of the wide sea, the South Wind (Šūtu) rose against him.

notes.official:
**Šūtu — the South Wind, divinized — rises against Adapa in the midst of the wide sea.** The DINGIR-determinative on *Šūtu* (cuneiform writing *IM.U18.LU*) marks the wind as a **divine being** — one of the four named cardinal winds (Šūtu south, Iltānu north, Šadû east, Amurru west) of the Akkadian meteorological-divine vocabulary. See new central entry `shutu-cardinal-winds-akkadian-four-winds-divinized-cross-corpus`. The South Wind is feminine in Akkadian gender; subsequent verbs (B:8 *uṭebbi-šu* 'she sank him'; B:46 *i-ziq-am-ma elippī ú-ṭe-eb-bi* 'she blew and she sank my boat') track the feminine pronoun.

Cross-corpus the Hebrew four-winds tradition (*arba ruchot ha-shamayim* — Jer 49:36, Ezek 37:9, Zech 6:5, Dan 7:2). The Hebrew tradition retains the four-cardinal-winds cosmographic-structure but de-divinizes the winds; they are agents-of-Yahweh, not deities-in-their-own-right. The shift is one of the diagnostic theological-moves in the Mesopotamian → Hebrew transition. **Operational disavowal**: no Sitchin-corpus reading of Šūtu as engineered-atmospheric-disturbance-technology; the personification is the standard Mesopotamian theological-mythological register.

lines.translit: elippa-šu uṭebbi-šu Adapa ana bīt nūni iṭṭebi-šu

i18n.en: She sank his boat; Adapa she thrust down into the house of the fish.

notes.official: The South Wind sinks Adapa's boat; she thrusts him down into *bīt nūni* 'the house of the fish' — the poetic-kenning for the watery-depths. See overlay entry `bit-nuni-house-of-the-fish-belly-of-the-deep-adapa`. Cross-corpus the Jonah-belly-of-the-fish image (Jon 1:17–2:10) as the closest Hebrew structural-parallel: a divinely-disturbed human plunged into the deep / fish-realm, surviving by divine-mercy or speech-act.

i18n.en: (He cried out:) 'South Wind, […] — South Wind, let me see your demon-form!'

notes.official: *(d)Šūta lūmur šēd-ki* 'O South Wind, let me see your *šēdu* (tutelary-spirit / demon-form)!' Adapa, angered by the sinking, challenges the wind to show its *šēdu* — its tutelary-spirit-form. The Akkadian *šēdu* is the protective-spirit / demon-form noun; cross-corpus the **direct Akkadian → Hebrew loanword** *shedim* (Deut 32:17, Ps 106:37). See new central entry `shedu-lamassu-tutelary-spirit-akkadian-hebrew-shedim-cross-corpus`. The semantic-shift from Akkadian morally-neutral *šēdu* (tutelary-spirit) to Hebrew pejorative *shedim* (foreign-cult-spirit / demonic-deity) is one of the diagnostic Akkadian → Hebrew loanword-domestications.

i18n.en: 'May I break your wing!' — by the word of his mouth.

notes.official:
**The speech-act-efficacy thesis-line of the composition.** *kappi-ki lu-uš-bi-ir aššum amat pī-šu* 'may I break your wing — by the word of his mouth.' Adapa, a human, breaks the wing of an immortal wind-deity **by speech alone**. Izre'el 2001's modern critical edition bears the subtitle *Language Has the Power of Life and Death*; the thesis is grounded in this verse. The preposition *aššum* 'because of, by means of' + construct *amat pī-šu* 'word of his mouth' is the explicit speech-act-instrumental: the wing breaks **because of / by means of** the word of his mouth. See new central entry `speech-act-efficacy-language-power-of-life-and-death-cross-corpus`.

Cross-corpus the Akkadian Marduk-creation-by-speech at Enuma Elish IV.19-26 (Marduk destroys-and-recreates a garment by spoken word); the Hebrew creation-by-divine-speech at Gen 1 (*va-yomer Elohim ... va-yhi-khen*); the Hebrew prophetic-word-as-efficacious-action at Isa 55:11 (the word that does not return empty); the proverbial Prov 18:21 *mavet ve-chayyim be-yad lashon* 'death and life are in the power of the tongue' (arguably the closest Hebrew parallel to Izre'el's subtitle). The wing-image is documented in overlay entry `kappi-wing-of-shutu-the-wing-breaking-image-adapa`. **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Christian-Johannine *Logos* pre-resolution (John 1:1-3 is the downstream Greek-philosophical-Wisdom synthesis of the Hebrew creation-by-speech tradition); (ii) no WoH-spin on Adapa-as-wielder-of-Elohim-engineered-vocal-technology; the speech-act-efficacy is theological-mythological, not technological-engineering.

lines.translit: ki-i ša ina pī-šu iqbû kapp(i) Šūti is-sa-bir
lines.cuneiform: 𒆠𒄿 𒊭 𒀸 𒉿𒋗  𒄿  𒄑𒊓𒄵

i18n.en: As he had spoken with his mouth, the wing of the South Wind was broken.

notes.official: *ki-i ša ina pī-šu iqbû kapp(i) Šūti is-sa-bir* 'as he had spoken with his mouth, the wing of the South Wind was broken'. The speech-act takes effect (passive perfect-verb *issabir* 'was broken'). The narrative-affirmation of the speech-act-efficacy thesis: the spoken word effects cosmic reality with material consequence.

lines.translit: sebet ūmī Šūtu ana māti ul iziq

i18n.en: For seven days the South Wind did not blow upon the land.

notes.official: *sebet ūmī Šūtu ana māti ul iziq* 'for seven days the South Wind did not blow upon the land'. The cosmic-disturbance from Adapa's curse: the wind-cessation registers in the heavenly-court (Anu inquires at B:13). The seven-day cosmic-marker is the same structural-numeral as the seven-day flood-storm in the Mesopotamian flood-traditions (Sumerian Flood Story D:3; Atrahasis III.iv.24-25; Gilgamesh XI.128) — see central entry `seven-day-flood-vs-forty-day-flood-duration-tradition-cross-corpus`, here extended to Adapa-side activation. The seven-day pattern recurs across Mesopotamian narrative-time-vocabulary (mourning, creation-week, etc.).

i18n.en: Anu addressed a word to Ilabrat his vizier:

notes.official: Anu addresses his vizier (*sukkallu*) Ilabrat. The *sukkallu* divine-vizier-office is one of the standard Mesopotamian divine-bureaucratic roles: each high-god has a vizier-intermediary (Anu has Ilabrat / Ninshubur / Papsukkal; Enlil has Nuska; Enki/Ea has Isimud/Usmu). See overlay entry `ilabrat-sukkallu-anu-vizier-adapa`. Cross-corpus, the structural-parallel to Hebrew angelic-intermediary figures (the *mal'akh YHWH* tradition; the named-angels Gabriel and Michael in Daniel) is functional-thematic.

lines.translit: mīnâ Šūtu ūmišamma ana māti ul iziq

i18n.en: 'Why has the South Wind not blown upon the land these days?'

notes.official: Anu's question: why has the South Wind not blown? The narrative-mechanism for moving the cosmic-disturbance from earth-level to heavenly-court-level: the wind-cessation is anomalous enough that the sky-god takes notice.

i18n.en: Ilabrat the vizier answered him:

notes.official: Ilabrat's answer follows.

lines.translit: bēlī Adapa māru ša Ea kappi Šūti iš-bir

i18n.en: 'My lord, Adapa, son of Ea, has broken the wing of the South Wind.'

notes.official: Ilabrat reports: 'My lord, Adapa son of Ea has broken the wing of the South Wind.' The vizier's report names the human-agent and the speech-act-effect. Adapa's *māru ša Ea* 'son of Ea' epithet here is the apkallu-paradigm-link to his master.

i18n.en: […] Anu heard, and his anger rose up.

notes.official: Anu's anger rises. The standard Mesopotamian divine-anger-response to cosmic-disturbance; the *uggata* 'anger' is the divine-court's affective-state.

lines.translit: lišēriba-šu lišā ana mahar-ya — qiba ana Adapa

i18n.en: 'Let them bring him up; let him come into my presence! Speak (the summons) to Adapa!'

notes.official: Anu's summons: 'Let them bring him up; let him come into my presence! Speak (the summons) to Adapa!' The verb *lišēriba-šu* 'let them bring him up' is the cosmographic-ascent verb (*šērubu* Š-stem of *erēbu* 'to enter / cause-to-enter'; the directional-implication is upward to the heavenly-court). See new central entry `human-ascent-to-heaven-adapa-etana-enoch-elijah-cross-corpus` on the broader ascent-motif.

lines.translit: (d)Ea apkal Eridu(KI) idī šipra ša šamê

i18n.en: Ea, the sage of Eridu, knew the (whole) work of heaven.

notes.official: *Ea apkal Eridu(KI) idī šipra ša šamê* 'Ea, the sage of Eridu, knew the (whole) work of heaven'. The *apkal* (apkallu) Ea is the divine-sage; Adapa is the human-apkallu (see central entry `adapa-apkallu-first-antediluvian-sage-paradigm-cross-corpus`). Ea anticipates the summons — *idī šipra ša šamê* 'he knew the work of heaven' — and prepares Adapa with the coaching-instruction (B:20-34). Ea's anticipatory-knowledge is one of the data-points relevant to the central interpretive-crux: did Ea *know* what Anu would offer? — see central entry `ea-warning-deception-misadvice-test-crux-cross-corpus`.

lines.translit: Adapa qarrāda iddi-šu-ma qarrāda mali kāspa idki-šu

i18n.en: He put Adapa in dishevelled (mourning) hair; he clothed him in mourning-garments.

notes.official: Ea instructs Adapa to appear in mourning-garb — dishevelled mourning-hair (*qarrāda*) and mourning-garments (*kāspa*). See new central entry `mourning-garb-dishevelled-hair-sackcloth-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus the Hebrew *sak ve-efer* sackcloth-and-ashes tradition (Gen 37:34, 2 Sam 3:31, Esth 4:1, Dan 9:3, Jonah 3:5-8). The ruse is that Adapa is to claim he mourns the *absent* Dumuzi and Gizzida — the gate-keepers themselves, who will be flattered (see central entry `dumuzi-tammuz-adonis-dying-and-rising-vegetation-god-cross-corpus`).

i18n.en: To Adapa Ea set down (the following) words:

notes.official: *ana Adapa Ea amāta išakkan* 'to Adapa Ea set down (the following) words'. The performative speech-frame opens the Ea-coaching-speech (B:21-34) — the formal master-to-disciple coaching-speech genre. See overlay entry `ea-instruction-coaching-speech-form-adapa`. The construction *amāta išakkan* 'set down (binding) words' is one of the diagnostic Akkadian-performative-speech vocabularies; the speech that follows binds Adapa to the protocol.

lines.translit: Adapa ana mahar (d)Anu šarri ana šamê tellû

i18n.en: 'Adapa, you are about to ascend to heaven, into the presence of Anu the king.'

notes.official: **Adapa's ascent to heaven.** *ana mahar (d)Anu šarri ana šamê tellû* 'you are about to ascend to heaven, into the presence of Anu the king'. See new central entry `human-ascent-to-heaven-adapa-etana-enoch-elijah-cross-corpus`. The cross-corpus motif cluster: Etana (Old Babylonian; ascent on the eagle for the plant-of-birth); Hanokh/Enoch (Gen 5:24 + 1 Enoch's full heavenly-ascent narrative); Eliyahu/Elijah (2 Kgs 2:11 the whirlwind-ascent); Isaiah-Ezekiel throne-visions (Isa 6, Ezek 1, 8-11, 40-48); the Hekhalot-merkavah Late-Antique reception; Paul's *third heaven* (2 Cor 12:1-4). **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Sitchin-corpus reading of the ascent as space-flight to an Anunnaki orbital installation; the Akkadian *elû ana šamê* is the theological-mythological *upward-to-the-divine-realm* vocabulary, not technological-engineering vocabulary; (ii) no Christian-Pauline-soteriology pre-resolution.

lines.translit: ina kâdi ša bāb šamê (d)Dumuzi u (d)Gizzida izzazzū
lines.cuneiform: 𒀸  𒊭 𒉽  𒀭 𒌋 𒀭

i18n.en: 'At the threshold of heaven's gate, Dumuzi and Gizzida stand watch.'

notes.official:
**Dumuzi and Gizzida — the gate-keeping deities of heaven.** *(d)Dumuzi u (d)Gizzida izzazzū* 'Dumuzi and Gizzida stand watch at the threshold of heaven's gate'. Dumuzi (Sum. Dumuzid, *dumu-zi-(d)* 'the rightful son'; the shepherd-god; Inana's consort; the dying-and-rising vegetation-deity) and Gizzida (Sum. Ningišzida, *nin-gish-zi-(d)-da* 'lord of the steadfast/rightful tree'; the chthonic-vegetation-and-snake god) are the two quintessential dying-and-rising vegetation-deities. See new central entry `dumuzi-tammuz-adonis-dying-and-rising-vegetation-god-cross-corpus`.

Cross-corpus, *Dumuzi* is the **direct etymological cognate** of Hebrew *Tammuz* (Ezek 8:14 *m'vakkot et ha-Tammuz* 'weeping for the Tammuz' at the Jerusalem temple-gate; the Hebrew month-name Tammuz is the cult-calendar fossil); Greek *Adonis* (West-Semitic *adon* 'lord' as divine-title); Phoenician Eshmun; Egyptian Osiris. **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Christian-resurrection-typology pre-resolution; the Frazer-tradition collapse of dying-and-rising-gods into a single archetype is heavily critiqued (Mettinger 2001; J. Z. Smith 1990); (ii) no WoH-spin on Dumuzi-as-engineered-immortal-prototype.

lines.translit: kī immarū-ka — ʾalka? ammīni? aššum manni?

i18n.en: 'When they see you they will ask — Where (are you bound)? Why? On whose account?'

notes.official: Ea's coaching continues: 'When they see you, they will ask — Where (are you bound)? Why? On whose account?' The three-question-formula is the standard heavenly-court intercession-screening protocol; Adapa must answer adroitly.

i18n.en: 'Lay a sweet word before them.'

notes.official: 'Lay a sweet word before them' — the diplomacy-protocol for the gate-keepers' intercession-favor. *amāta tâbta* 'sweet word' (*amāta* + adj. *ṭâbtu* 'sweet, good') is the formal-diplomatic phrase.

lines.translit: ašalūki — ana ilī šina ša ina mātīni iḫalliqū

i18n.en: 'I will go (to mourn) — on account of the two gods who have vanished from our land.'

notes.official: Ea's coached-answer for Adapa: 'I will go (to mourn) — on account of the two gods who have vanished from our land.' The reference is to Dumuzi and Gizzida — the dying-and-rising vegetation-deities whose **annual seasonal disappearance from the land** (the dry season; vegetation withered) is the cult-mourning occasion. The flattering ambiguity: Adapa is told to claim he mourns these two gods; the gate-keepers themselves are these gods, and will receive cult-recognition from the mourner.

lines.translit: kī iqabbi-ka — mannu šunu? Adapa — Dumuzi u Gizzida

i18n.en: 'When they ask you — Who are they? (You shall say:) Dumuzi and Gizzida.'

notes.official: 'When they ask — Who are they? — (you shall say:) Dumuzi and Gizzida.' Adapa is to confess the names — naming the gate-keepers themselves as the mourned-deities. The flattery is now-explicit.

lines.translit: iḫdū-ma ana mahar Anu damiqta iqabbū-ka

i18n.en: 'They will rejoice, and before Anu they will speak a good word on your behalf.'

notes.official: Ea predicts the outcome: 'They will rejoice, and before Anu they will speak a good word on your behalf.' The gate-keepers' intercession will pacify Anu's anger.

i18n.en: 'Anu will (then) cause his favorable face to pass over you.'

notes.official: 'Anu will (then) cause his favorable face to pass over you' — the divine-favor formula. The *favorable face* (*pānū damqu*) is the standard Mesopotamian divine-pleasure indicator; cross-corpus the Hebrew *yaer panav* 'cause his face to shine upon you' (Num 6:25 priestly blessing) is the functional-parallel of divine-favor-facing.

lines.translit: ina mahar Anu izziz-ma akala ša mūti ukallū-ka — ul takkala
lines.cuneiform: 𒀸 𒅆 𒀭 𒈠  𒊭  𒅗  𒌌

i18n.en: 'When you stand before Anu, they will offer you the bread of death — do not eat (it).'

notes.official:
**The Ea-warning crux — the central interpretive crux of the composition.** *akala ša mūti ukallū-ka — ul takkala* 'they will offer you the bread of death — do not eat (it).' Whether Ea **deliberately deceives** Adapa to prevent humanity from gaining immortality, **was himself mistaken** about the funerary-protocol substances offered to a mortal visitor in Anu's court, or **strategically tests** Adapa's obedience-to-the-master's-word is the central interpretive-crux of the entire poem. Three named-scholarship readings — Lambert / Kvanvig (deliberate-deception); Buccellati / Bing (unintentional-misadvice); Izre'el (strategic-test) — are presented in full at the new central entry `ea-warning-deception-misadvice-test-crux-cross-corpus`. The Editor does **not adjudicate** between the three readings.

Cross-corpus, the Adapa B:30-31 crux has a structural-parallel in Gen 3's *eat-or-not-eat-the-fruit* crux: the serpent's *lo mot temutun* 'you shall not surely die' (Gen 3:4) contradicts Yahweh's *mot tamut* 'you shall surely die' (Gen 2:17). The Adapa-Eden inverse-pattern: in Adapa, the human's **trusted figure** (Ea, the master) **possibly deceives**, and the human obeys; in Eden, the human's **adversarial figure** (the serpent) **possibly truth-tells**, and the humans disobey (Yahweh). Same end-state (humanity wisdom-bearing-but-mortal) via opposite trust-relations. **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Christian-Adamic-Fall pre-resolution; (ii) no WoH-spin on Ea-as-Anunnaki-rebel-keeping-humanity-mortal (the Sitchin-tradition reading); (iii) no Christian-Johannine *bread-of-life* (John 6:35,48) pre-resolution.

i18n.en: 'They will offer you the water of death — do not drink (it).'

notes.official: Parallel to B:30: *mê mūti ukallū-ka — ul tašatti* 'they will offer you the water of death — do not drink (it).' The water-of-death warning matches the bread-of-death warning. See central entry `ea-warning-deception-misadvice-test-crux-cross-corpus`. **Operational disavowal**: no Christian-Johannine *living-water* (John 4:10-14) pre-resolution.

i18n.en: 'They will offer you a garment — put it on.'

notes.official: 'They will offer you a garment — put it on.' The garment is **not** marked as deadly; Ea instructs Adapa to accept it. The selective-warning (food/water *deadly*; garment/oil *not-deadly*) is one of the data-points supporting the deliberate-deception reading of the Ea-warning crux. See overlay entry `anointing-and-garment-non-deadly-accompaniments-adapa`.

i18n.en: 'They will offer you oil — anoint yourself (with it).'

notes.official: 'They will offer you oil — anoint yourself (with it).' The oil is **not** marked as deadly. The Akkadian *šamna pussis* anointing-vocabulary is the cognate of Hebrew *shemen* + *mashach* (the anointing-with-oil cult-rite; 1 Sam 16:13 David's anointing; Ex 30:22-33 the priestly anointing-oil; the *mashiach* 'anointed-one' title). The selective-warning sharpens the deliberate-deception reading. See overlay entry `anointing-and-garment-non-deadly-accompaniments-adapa`.

lines.translit: ṭēmu ša aqbâ-kum la teggâ — amāt ša aqbâ-kum ukāl
lines.cuneiform: 𒊭 𒄣 𒆷   𒊩𒆳 𒊭 𒄣

i18n.en: 'The instruction I have given you, do not transgress; the word I have given you, hold fast.'

notes.official: *ṭēmu ša aqbâ-kum la teggâ — amāt ša aqbâ-kum ukāl* 'the instruction I have given you, do not transgress; the word I have given you, hold fast.' The closing of Ea's coaching-speech: the binding-of-the-disciple-to-the-master's-word. The verb *egû* 'to transgress / be negligent' is the technical-vocabulary of disciple-obedience; the *kullu / ukāl* 'hold fast' is the master's binding-imperative. Cross-corpus the Hebrew *shamar* 'to keep, observe' commandment-keeping vocabulary (Deut 6:17). The Ea-instruction's force is what makes Adapa's later refusal of the food-of-life (B:55-56) the cosmic-act-of-obedience that resolves the narrative.

lines.translit: tâbi(?) ša Eridu Adapa illika ana šamê i-ti-li

i18n.en: The good one of Eridu — Adapa — went; to heaven he ascended.

notes.official: Adapa ascends. *ana šamê i-ti-li* 'to heaven he ascended' — the second ascent-attestation in the chapter (after B:22). See central entry `human-ascent-to-heaven-adapa-etana-enoch-elijah-cross-corpus`.

lines.translit: ina kâdi ša bāb Anu Dumuzi u Gizzida i-ta-tu-šú
lines.cuneiform: 𒀸  𒊭 𒉽 𒀭  𒌋  𒄿𒋫𒌅

i18n.en: At the threshold of Anu's gate, Dumuzi and Gizzida caught sight of him.

notes.official: Dumuzi and Gizzida catch sight of Adapa at the threshold of Anu's gate. The gate-keeper-encounter that Ea predicted now unfolds.

lines.translit: Adapa ammīni qarrāda u kāspu tu-na-as-saḫ?

i18n.en: 'Adapa — why have you taken on dishevelled hair and mourning-garment?'

notes.official: The gate-keepers ask: 'Adapa — why have you taken on dishevelled hair and mourning-garment?' The *qarrāda u kāspu* mourning-pair (see central entry `mourning-garb-dishevelled-hair-sackcloth-cross-corpus`) elicits the gate-keepers' inquiry exactly as Ea predicted at B:24.

lines.translit: ina mātīni ilāni šina iḫliqū-ma ana-ku qarrāda lā nasḫāku

i18n.en: 'From our land two gods have vanished; therefore I (go) in dishevelled hair.'

notes.official: Adapa's coached-answer: 'From our land two gods have vanished; therefore I (go) in dishevelled hair.' The flattering-ambiguity Ea coached is delivered: Adapa speaks of Dumuzi and Gizzida (the seasonally-disappeared vegetation-deities), and the listeners are revealed as those very gods.

lines.translit: mannu šunu ilāni šina? — Dumuzi u Gizzida

i18n.en: 'Who are these two gods?' — 'Dumuzi and Gizzida.'

notes.official: 'Who are these two gods?' — 'Dumuzi and Gizzida.' The flattery is named.

i18n.en: They looked at one another; they smiled.

notes.official: *i-na-as-sa-ḫū-ma a-ḫa-iš ut-tab-bi-tu* 'they looked at one another; they smiled.' The flattery has worked; the gate-keepers will intercede for Adapa.

lines.translit: ana mahar Anu i-mu-uš-šu-ma damiqta iqabbū

i18n.en: Before Anu they came forward, and they spoke a good word (on his behalf).

notes.official: Before Anu, Dumuzi and Gizzida speak a good word on Adapa's behalf — the intercession Ea predicted at B:28.

i18n.en: Anu turned upon him his favorable face.

notes.official: Anu turns his favorable face upon Adapa — the divine-favor-facing formula (*pānū damqu*) that Ea predicted at B:29. The intercession-and-pacification sequence has worked as planned.

i18n.en: 'Adapa — why did you break the wing of the South Wind?'

notes.official: Anu's confrontation-question: 'Adapa — why did you break the wing of the South Wind?' The cosmic-disturbance Adapa caused at B:10-11 now requires explanation before the divine-court.

lines.translit: bēlī ina libbi tâmti ša rapaš-tum ana bīt bēlī-ya nūni a-ṣa-id
lines.cuneiform: 𒀸   𒊭 𒌈 𒁹 𒂍 𒉿  𒀀𒍝𒀉

i18n.en: 'My lord — in the midst of the wide sea, for my lord's house I was netting fish.'

notes.official: Adapa's defense: 'My lord — in the midst of the wide sea, for my lord's house I was netting fish.' Adapa frames the wing-breaking as a justified-response to the South Wind's unprovoked disruption of his cult-service-fishing for Ea's temple. The defense reasserts the apkallu's cult-loyalty.

i18n.en: 'The sea rose up like a (high) sanctuary-pavilion.'

notes.official: Adapa's account continues: 'The sea rose up like a (high) sanctuary-pavilion.' The storm-description; *ma-ha-zi-im* 'sanctuary-pavilion' is the cosmographic-figure for the sea's vertical-rise.

i18n.en: 'The South Wind blew, and she sank my boat.'

notes.official: 'The South Wind blew, and she sank my boat.' The feminine-pronoun tracks the South Wind's grammatical-gender (Akkadian *Šūtu* fem.).

lines.translit: ana bīt nūni it-ti-bi-(an)-ni — ina libbati-ya Šūta luš-bi-ir
lines.cuneiform: 𒁹 𒂍  𒀉𒋾𒁉𒀭𒉌  𒀸 𒉿  𒁉𒅕

i18n.en: 'She thrust me down into the house of the fish — in my anger I (cried out): May I break the South Wind!'

notes.official: Adapa's defense closes: 'She thrust me down into the house of the fish (*bīt nūni* — the deep) — in my anger I (cried out): May I break the South Wind!' Adapa names his speech-act-curse as anger-motivated; the defense is plausible.

i18n.en: Anu pondered (the matter) in his heart.

notes.official: Anu ponders the case in his heart — the divine-deliberation formula. *ina libbi-šu i-tap-pal* 'in his heart he answered (himself)' is the standard Mesopotamian self-deliberation locution.

lines.translit: Dumuzi u Gizzida ana Anu i-ma-an-nu-ma

i18n.en: Dumuzi and Gizzida recounted (his case) to Anu.

notes.official: Dumuzi and Gizzida recount Adapa's case to Anu — the gate-keepers' formal-intercession before the high-god.

lines.translit: Anu lib-ba-šu i-pa-šaḫ — ana mīna Ea pālīḫa ana mār ša awīluti tu-lap-pi-it?
lines.cuneiform: 𒀭 𒈜𒁀𒋗 𒄿𒉺  𒁹 𒈫 𒀀  𒁹 𒈥 𒊭  𒌅𒆗𒉿𒀉

i18n.en: Anu's heart grew calm. (He said:) 'Why did Ea reveal (the things) of heaven and earth to a son of humankind? Why did he set a strong heart upon him?'

notes.official:
**Anu's theodicy-question — the divine-secret-leak recognition.** Anu's heart is appeased; he asks: 'Why did Ea reveal (the things) of heaven and earth to a son of humankind? Why did he set a strong heart upon him?' The verb *lapātu* D-stem 'to reveal, make manifest' names Ea's action as a **transfer of divine-knowledge to the human-side of the divine-human divide**. See new central entry `divine-secret-leak-forbidden-knowledge-from-gods-to-humans-cross-corpus`.

Cross-corpus, the Anu-recognition at B:50 is the **same cosmic-moment** as the Yahweh-recognition at Gen 3:22 (*hen ha-adam hayah k-achad mimmennu la-da'at tov va-ra* — see existing central entry `ke-achad-mimmennu`): the divine-court's formal acknowledgement that a human has entered the divine-knowledge category. The Genesis sequel is the barring of the tree-of-life (Gen 3:22-24); the Adapa sequel is the offering of the food-of-life (B:51-52) — which Adapa refuses. Same divine-recognition-moment, structurally-different-divine-responses. The motif is wide cross-corpus: the Hebrew Watchers-tradition (1 Enoch 6-11; underlying Gen 6:1-4); the Greek Prometheus (Hesiod *Theogony* 535-616; Aeschylus *Prometheus Bound*). **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Sitchin-corpus reading of Ea-leaked-genetic-tech-to-humans; (ii) no Christian Eden-Fall typology pre-resolution; (iii) no Adapa-as-Adam identity claim.

lines.translit: šuāti mīnâ niqâb-šu? — akāl balāṭi liblū-šu — likul

i18n.en: 'As for him — what shall we (now) decree? Let them bring him the food of life; let him eat.'

notes.official:
**The ironic reversal — *akāl balāṭi* 'food of life'.** *šuāti mīnâ niqâb-šu? — akāl balāṭi liblū-šu — likul* 'As for him — what shall we (now) decree? Let them bring him the food of life; let him eat.' What Ea called *akāl mūti* 'food of death' (B:30) is in fact *akāl balāṭi* 'food of LIFE'. The construct *akāl balāṭi* (*akāl* 'food' + *balāṭi* gen. of *balāṭu* 'life') is the immortality-substance.

This is the cosmic-pivot of the composition: the substance-pair (food-and-water of life) would have made Adapa immortal had he eaten. See new central entry `akal-balati-me-balati-food-of-life-water-of-life-akkadian-hebrew-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus the Hebrew *etz ha-chayyim* 'tree of life' (Gen 2:9, 3:22; see existing entry `etz-chayim-daat`); Prov 3:18 wisdom-as-tree-of-life; Ezek 47:12 trees-of-life by the temple-river; Rev 22:1-2 tree-of-life. The inverse-parallel between Adapa (humanity *refuses* divine food, loses immortality) and Eden (humanity *eats* divine food, loses immortality) — same cosmic-result via opposite human-action — is the Heidel-Buccellati-Hallo-Kvanvig comparative-mythology framing. **Operational disavowals**: (i) no Christian-Johannine *bread-of-life* (John 6:48) pre-resolution; (ii) no WoH/Sitchin *engineered-immortality-substance* reading; (iii) no Adapa-as-Adam identity claim.

i18n.en: 'Let them bring him the water of life; let him drink.'

notes.official: Parallel to B:51: *mê balāṭi liblū-šu — lišti* 'let them bring him the water of life; let him drink.' The water-of-life pair with the food-of-life. **Operational disavowal**: no Christian-Johannine *living-water* (John 4:10-14; Rev 22:1) pre-resolution; the Adapa narrative is centuries earlier than the Johannine reception.

i18n.en: 'Let them bring him a garment; let him put it on.'

notes.official: 'Let them bring him a garment; let him put it on.' The non-deadly accompaniment — the garment is offered alongside the immortality-food-and-water. See overlay entry `anointing-and-garment-non-deadly-accompaniments-adapa`.

i18n.en: 'Let them bring him oil; let him anoint himself.'

notes.official: 'Let them bring him oil; let him anoint himself.' The non-deadly accompaniment — the anointing-with-oil cult-rite paralleling the Hebrew *mashach* tradition (1 Sam 16:13; Ex 30:22-33).

lines.translit: akāl balāṭi ana mahri-šu ub-lu-ma — Adapa ul ikkal

i18n.en: They brought the food of life before him — but Adapa did not eat.

notes.official:
**The moment of lost immortality.** *akāl balāṭi ana mahri-šu ub-lu-ma — Adapa ul ikkal* 'they brought the food of life before him — but Adapa did not eat.' Adapa, obeying Ea's coached warning, refuses what would have given him eternal life.

The inverse-parallel of Gen 3:6 (Eve eats the forbidden fruit and humanity becomes wisdom-bearing-but-mortal) and Gen 3:22-24 (the tree-of-life is then barred). In Adapa: human **refuses** the divine food and humanity is mortal. In Genesis: human **eats** the divine food and humanity is mortal. The two narratives encode the same theological end-state (humans wisdom-bearing-but-mortal) by opposite-direction stories. The cross-corpus pattern is documented from Heidel 1942 forward; the comparative-mythology framing is **named-scholarship** (Heidel; Buccellati 1973; Hallo 1969; Kvanvig 2011; Izre'el 2001), **not** identity-claim. See central entry `akal-balati-me-balati-food-of-life-water-of-life-akkadian-hebrew-cross-corpus`.

lines.translit: mê balāṭi ana mahri-šu ub-lu-ma — ul išatti

i18n.en: They brought the water of life before him — but he did not drink.

notes.official: Parallel to B:55: 'they brought the water of life before him — but he did not drink'.

lines.translit: lubuš ub-lu-ma — il-tab-aš — šamna ub-lu-ma — ip-ta-as-sa-as

i18n.en: They brought the garment — he put it on. They brought the oil — he anointed himself (with it).

notes.official: Adapa accepts the non-deadly gifts: garment (put it on); oil (anointed himself). The selective-obedience confirms his exact-compliance with Ea's coaching (accept what Ea said to accept; refuse what Ea said to refuse). See overlay entry `anointing-and-garment-non-deadly-accompaniments-adapa`.

i18n.en: Anu looked at him — and laughed.

notes.official:
**Anu looks at him and laughs.** *Anu īmur-šu-ma — i-ṣi-iḫ*. The Akkadian *ṣâḫu* 'to laugh, smile' is semantically open between three readings: (a) **derisive** laughter at Adapa (Lambert: Anu mocks the human who refused immortality); (b) **amused** laughter at Ea's craftiness (Foster: Anu acknowledges Ea has out-thought him); (c) **ironic-cosmic** laughter at the human-mortality comedy (Izre'el: the test has resolved as Ea designed it). The tone maps onto the three readings of the Ea-warning crux. See new central entry `divine-laughter-anu-laughs-sahaq-tsachu-cross-corpus`.

Cross-corpus, the Akkadian *ṣâḫu* and Hebrew *sahaq / tzachaq* are **Semitic cognates** (proto-Semitic *√ṣḥq); the Hebrew divine-laughter at Ps 2:4 (*yoshev ba-shamayim yischak Adonai yilag lamo* 'he who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord derides them'), Ps 37:13, Ps 59:8 is the closest Hebrew parallel. The same root yields the Yitzchaq/Isaac name-etymology (Gen 17:17, 18:12, 21:6). Greek *gelōs* (Homeric divine-laughter) is the wider comparandum.

lines.translit: alka — Adapa — ammīni la takkala la tašatti? — la baltāta?

i18n.en: 'Come now, Adapa — why did you not eat, why did you not drink? Are you (now) not to live?'

notes.official: Anu's confrontation-question: 'Come now, Adapa — why did you not eat, why did you not drink? Are you (now) not to live?' The verb *baltāta* (from *balāṭu* 'to live') in the predicate question *la baltāta?* explicitly confirms that the food and water were of **life** (*balāṭu*) — the explicit-reveal of the Ea-warning-crux. See central entry `ea-warning-deception-misadvice-test-crux-cross-corpus`.

lines.translit: Ea bēlī aqbâ — la takkala la tašatti

i18n.en: 'My lord Ea commanded me — Do not eat, do not drink.'

notes.official: Adapa names Ea as the source of his warning: 'My lord Ea commanded me — Do not eat, do not drink.' The naming of Ea closes the responsibility-loop: Adapa has acted in obedience to his master-deity; the cosmic-result is the master-deity's responsibility. The narrative leaves the question of Ea's *motive* unresolved — the central interpretive-crux remains open.

i18n.en: 'Take him; return him to his earth.'

notes.official:
**The mortality-verdict — return to the earth.** *leqâ-šu — ana erṣeti-šu utīrā-šu* 'take him — return him to his earth'. Anu's closing command sends Adapa back from the heavenly-court to the human-earth realm — back to the mortal-human condition, eventually to the netherworld-earth at death.

Cross-corpus Hebrew Gen 3:19 *ki afar attah ve-el afar tashuv* 'for you are dust, and to dust you shall return'. The Akkadian *târu* D-stem 'return / send back' + *ana erṣeti-šu* 'to his earth' is the structural-and-lexical parallel of the Hebrew *shuv* 'return' + *el ha-adamah* / *el afar* 'to the ground / to the dust'. Both narratives close with the explicit divine-decree of human-return-to-the-earth as the cosmic-resolution of the wisdom-immortality-decoupling. See new central entry `return-to-the-earth-mortality-verdict-adapa-genesis-cross-corpus`.

notes.official: Fragment D is small but preserves the **catchline** — the formula identifying the next composition in the scribal-series. Catchlines in Mesopotamian scribal-practice are the closing-formulas that link tablets in a series (cf. Gilgamesh's Standard Babylonian catchlines). The Adapa catchline is documented in Lambert 1976 and Izre'el 2001; the specific catchline-reading is pending verification in this pass. See overlay entry `catchline-and-fragmentary-fragments-cd-disclosure-adapa`.
